newsitem.title: USA: Hormel sees grain, hog pressures easing.
newsitem.headline: Hormel sees grain, hog pressures easing.

text.p: Hormel Foods Corp said Wednesday that high prices for grain and hogs, which pressured its profit margins in fiscal 1996, are easing.

"The major problems of the past year, prices for grain and live hog commodities, are, by their nature, cyclical and show signs of abating," Joel Johnson, chairman, said in a statement. "We remain focused on our proven strategic initiatives and look optimistically to the year ahead."
Earlier, Hormel reported earnings for the fourth quarter ended October 26 of $0.40 a share, after a $0.07 charge, down from $0.50 a year ago.
The fourth quarter charge related to the company's decision to exit its catfish business.
For fiscal 1996, it earned $1.04 a share, down from $1.57.

"As stated in our second and third quarter reports, a combination of extraordinarily high grain costs, higher than anticipated live hog prices and competing low-priced meat alternative were factors that depressed earnings for much of the year," Johnson said.
Despite the profit pressures, Hormel said it maintained or expanded the market share of core branded products while introducing new meat and food products.

Separately, Hormel said it distributed $7,461,000 to its employees as part of its voluntary profit sharing program. Under the profit sharing distribution, which is paid at the discretion of the board of directors, each eligible employee received an average the equivalent of 2.18 extra base weekly paychecks.
Hormel is a meat and food processor.
